messages.subject: PCA plot....only frame certain groups
parts:
Hi Everyone, 

I've recently tried to run and plot a PCA based on certain gene content. I've used prcomp to run PCA analysis and autoplot for plotting. To help visualize the different groups, I turned frame to TRUE. However, I realized that I have two large groups (E,U) that I want to mask the framing of. I've tried to google a solution but haven't found anything yet. 

Has anyone here have a solution to plot pca analysis with framing but not to all groups?

Here's the code snip (though not sure if it is useful for this question):
pca <- autoplot(prcomp(pca_gene_content[,1:49]), main = "CAZyme plot", frame = T ,data = pca_gene_content, colour = "Species", size = 4, label = T) + theme_bw()

And here's a picture of the plot below for reference.



Thanks so much for your help!!!
Dani

--
Danielle (Dani) Stevens
Ph.D. Student | Integrative Genetics & Genomics
Coaker Lab | UC Davis Plant Pathology

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: PCA plot....only frame certain groups
parts:
Hi Danielle

This is a tricky question. Usually, ggplot2 has the nice %+% operator, that allows to recall a plot with a different/subset of the data. Unfortunately, it does not seem to work here. Only way found was to do a heavy hack into the function: basically looking at ggfortify:::autoplot.prcomp, you see that you need to subset/filter the first line to get your result: plot.data <- ggplot2::fortify(object, data = data)

See code below, with a reproducible example (you could just have checked the help page of autoplot.prcomp for a reproducible example):

library(tidyverse)
library(ggfortify)

fo <- function (object, data = NULL, scale = 1, x = 1, y = 2, variance_percentage = TRUE, 
          ..., subset_cond= NULL) 
{
  plot.data <- ggplot2::fortify(object, data = data)

  if(!rlang::quo_is_null(enquo(subset_cond))) {
    plot.data <- filter(plot.data, {{subset_cond}})  
  }


  plot.data$rownames <- rownames(plot.data)
  if (is_derived_from(object, "prcomp")) {
    ve <- object$sdev^2/sum(object$sdev^2)
    PC <- paste0("PC", c(x, y))
    x.column <- PC[1]
    y.column <- PC[2]
    loadings.column <- "rotation"
    lam <- object$sdev[c(x, y)]
    lam <- lam * sqrt(nrow(plot.data))
  }
  else if (is_derived_from(object, "princomp")) {
    ve <- object$sdev^2/sum(object$sdev^2)
    PC <- paste0("Comp.", c(x, y))
    x.column <- PC[1]
    y.column <- PC[2]
    loadings.column <- "loadings"
    lam <- object$sdev[c(x, y)]
    lam <- lam * sqrt(nrow(plot.data))
  }
  else if (is_derived_from(object, "factanal")) {
    if (is.null(attr(object, "covariance"))) {
      p <- nrow(object$loading)
      ve <- colSums(object$loading^2)/p
    }
    else ve <- NULL
    PC <- paste0("Factor", c(x, y))
    x.column <- PC[1]
    y.column <- PC[2]
    scale <- 0
    loadings.column <- "loadings"
  }
  else if (is_derived_from(object, "lfda")) {
    ve <- NULL
    PC <- paste0("PC", c(x, y))
    x.column <- PC[1]
    y.column <- PC[2]
    scale <- 0
    loadings.column <- NULL
  }
  else {
    stop(paste0("Unsupported class for autoplot.pca_common: ", 
                class(object)))
  }

  if (scale != 0) {
    lam <- lam^scale
    plot.data[, c(x.column, y.column)] <- t(t(plot.data[, 
                                                        c(x.column, y.column)])/lam)
  }
  plot.columns <- unique(c(x.column, y.column, colnames(plot.data)))
  plot.data <- plot.data[, plot.columns]
  if (!is.null(loadings.column)) {
    loadings.data <- as.data.frame(object[[loadings.column]][, 
                                                             ])
    loadings.data$rownames <- rownames(loadings.data)
    loadings.columns <- unique(c(x.column, y.column, colnames(loadings.data)))
    loadings.data <- loadings.data[, loadings.columns]
  }
  else {
    loadings.data <- NULL
  }
  if (is.null(ve) | !variance_percentage) {
    labs <- PC
  }
  else {
    ve <- ve[c(x, y)]
    labs <- paste0(PC, " (", round(ve * 100, 2), "%)")
  }
  xlab <- labs[1]
  ylab <- labs[2]

  p <- ggbiplot(plot.data = plot.data, loadings.data = loadings.data, 
                xlab = xlab, ylab = ylab, ...)
  return(p)
}

environment(fo) <-  environment(ggbiplot)

fo(stats::prcomp(iris[-5]),
              data =iris,
              colour = 'Species',
              label=TRUE, frame=TRUE)


fo(stats::prcomp(iris[-5]),
   data =iris,
   subset_cond= Species!="setosa",
   colour = 'Species',
   label=TRUE, frame=TRUE)
